title: Inventory-driven compatibility declaration and minimum runtime assertions for new open weights
creator: Asha Nair
description: Clarify and formalize a lightweight, inventory-driven compatibility declaration that model authors submit with open weights and define the minimum runtime assertions Redwood must automatically validate before allowing catalog ingress or a soft unpinned rollout. Goal: reduce manual review friction for low-risk entrants while preserving production safety and clear rollback criteria.
background: We receive many community model submissions with inconsistent metadata. Current intake relies on manual checks and ad-hoc runtime annotations which increase triage latency. Engineering has implemented runtime probes and a compatibility scoring endpoint, but product and intake flow lack a prescriptive contract. This ticket defines the contract between the intake form, the model manifest, and the runtime validation checks that gate staged rollout and pinning decisions.
proposed_requirements: Define a minimal compatibility manifest schema (format + required fields) that is prefilled by the intake UI: runtime_architecture, expected_max_seq_len, kv_cache_hint, quantized_variants_available, cpu_fallback_ok, critical_ops_list.

Supply an 'inventory fingerprint' generated by the intake system that maps model manifest fields to runtime capability checks (for example: attention kernel compatibility, pos-enc type check, required BLAS kernels).

Add an automated 'manifest -> runtime probe' step that runs a lightweight smoke inference job (sample prompt, 8 tokens generation, validate shape/latency/kv behavior) in a sandbox to produce a verification report URL.

Define minimum pass/fail thresholds for automatic admission to 'unpinned canary' (e.g., smoke run complete without kernel errors, tail latency < 3x median host latency, KV cache hit correctness on 5-prefix tests).
If the manifest declares cpu_fallback_ok=false then require 2 additional runtime sanity runs on dedicated GPU profile before admission.
Add an explicit 'soft-pin exemption' flag that product can approve for models that pass automated checks but lack a long-term pin decision; exemptions expire in 90 days unless hard pin approved.
Document required fields and their acceptable values in the intake UI with inline help and examples for common open model families.
Expose the compatibility score and smoke verification report as part of the catalog entry page in the Console and the intake review queue for SEs/PMs.

Define a minimal rollback and fallback policy: any model that fails its smoke verification in production must be automatically routed to a pinned, vetted variant (if available) or removed from canary traffic and flagged urgent for the runtime on-call team.
Create metrics to track intake time, automated verification pass rate, and median time-to-pinning decision.
Ensure policy can be overridden by security_review_required flag for models with attached enterprise data requirements.
Include a backward-compatible mode for previously ingested models so we can re-run the verification without changing user-visible identifiers.
Provide clear acceptance tests and a migration path for older catalog entries to adopt the new manifest fields.
Deliver a concise PRD section for developer docs and the intake UI copy updates.
scope_changes: This PRD narrows the previous broad 'compat matrix' work to a minimal, inventory-driven contract for intake and runtime smoke checks. Out of scope: full deterministic kernel selection, quantization tuning automation, and runtime-driven auto-pin decisions (those will be follow-up epics).
decisions: 1) Adopt an intake-first schema: manifest fields become the source-of-truth for automated probes. 2) Automated smoke verification is required for unpinned canary admission; it is not sufficient for permanent pinning. 3) Soft-pin exemptions are allowed with a 90-day expiration. 4) Security-critical models require manual security_review_required signoff regardless of automated pass.
acceptance_criteria: Intake UI enforces required manifest fields and validates format on submit.
Automated smoke verification executes in sandbox and returns a verification report URL for every new open model submission within 30 minutes of intake.
At least 85% of new submissions pass automated smoke verification in staging (measured over a 2-week window) and failures are triaged into the intake queue with root-cause categories.
Console shows compatibility score and link to verification report on the model catalog entry page.
Soft-pin exemption flow exists: PMs can mark an entry exempt and the exemption record includes expiry date and reason.
Rollback path implemented: failing canary traffic for a model triggers automatic re-routing to a pinned variant or removes model from canary and creates an urgent incident ticket in the intake board.
Documentation updated: intake guide, manifest schema reference, and runbook for on-call are published and linked from the intake queue.
Automation tests cover the manifest validation, smoke verification happy path, and a simulated failure that exercises the rollback rule.
Stakeholder approvals: PM, Runtime Eng, Platform Security have sign-off recorded in comments.
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (staged): 2-week beta where only models created by internal teams and pilot partners go through the new manifest + smoke verification. Monitor metrics and gather feedback.
Phase 2 (wider): open intake enabled for public submissions with soft-pin exemptions allowed. Increase verification infra capacity as needed.
Phase 3 (enforce): require manifest and verification report for any new unpinned canary admission; after 30 days, require re-verification for unpinned entries older than 90 days.
Phase 4 (migrate): run a backfill job to re-verify existing catalog entries and surface older entries that need manual attention.
test_plan: Test plan consists of unit tests for manifest schema validation, e2e tests that submit a model manifest and assert a verification report is generated, and chaos tests that simulate kernel-load errors during smoke runs to verify rollback behavior. Performance tests: ensure smoke verification completes within 30 minutes under expected intake load. Acceptance automation includes a harness that replays 50 past model manifests with known good/bad characteristics.
notes: Initial runtime probe implementation is up-to-date with latest kernel telemetry (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/647).
We will reuse existing ingestion bucket and add a 'verification-reports' prefix.
Design research: intake UI samples are in Google Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1-intake-ui-samples
